01.title: Durable workflow foundation
implemented_capabilities: six HTTP endpoints
versioned normalized idempotency
atomic workflow/task/event creation
row-locked idempotent cancellation
snapshot details
event cursor pagination
bounded readiness and request contexts
graceful shutdown
explicit Goose migrations
disposable PostgreSQL verification
decisions: Empty project initialized as a standalone Git repository; unrelated parent files preserved
Task definitions do not execute; no attempt/scheduler/broker/agent/frontend
Normalization v1 frozen by golden hash; future fields require explicit retry compatibility
Workflow version is event sequence only for stage-01 mutations; future history requires a serialized allocator
Task unique indexes and event primary key cover workflow FK/update/order predicates; no redundant indexes
Verification owns uniquely named labelled disposable containers; development storage never destroyed
Generated sanitized logs replaced on rerun and ignored; progress and evidence excluded from fingerprint
Official pgx, PostgreSQL, net/http, Goose and Docker image documentation consulted
Windows race tests use pinned Linux Go image; smoke runs Linux API containers to verify real SIGTERM draining

02.title: Persisted DAG scheduler
implemented_capabilities: validated immutable DAG and bounded graph snapshot API
normalization-v2 and frozen legacy-v1 retry compatibility
additive composite-FK migration and serialized event allocator
bounded database-locked reconciliation and scan rotation
failure propagation with independent branches and terminal aggregation
scheduler process with contexts, shutdown and sanitized logs
deterministic graph/property tests and real PostgreSQL concurrency/upgrade tests
real scheduler kill/restart, diamond fixture and outage verification
decisions: Use the checked-out ForgeSwarm repository; existing changes are preserved
Stage 01 acceptance and baseline builds are verified before Stage 02 changes; current Git revision is recorded below
Dependency order semantically irrelevant; duplicates invalid; display order preserved. Kahn validation O(V+E), sorting only for normalization
New creations store normalization v2; explicit empty dependencies match legacy v1, nonempty edges conflict with legacy keys
No applied migration edited; migration 00002 backfills event sequence while parent DDL lock excludes old history writers
Upgrade API after migration before starting scheduler; old binary cancellation cannot allocate the new history sequence
Definitions and edges finalize atomically with workflow.created and are guarded against later SQL mutation
Parent locks before child states/history; version increments once per mutation, sequence once per event; no runtime MAX(sequence)+1
Continue independent branches; failure terminal only when unfinished/runnable/running work is terminal; READY never counts as success
Per-workflow serialization and bounded batch locks trade throughput for consistency; SKIP LOCKED has no strict fairness under persistent contention
Oldest persisted scheduler_checked_at rotates no-op scans without mutating public state/revision/timestamps
FAILED/BLOCKED and individually CANCELLED predecessors are unsuccessful and block unfinished descendants; whole-workflow cancellation wins by transaction order
No production terminal setter, claim/executor/broker/LLM/dynamic DAG. RUNNING is only a state-machine boundary for Stage 03
Stage-01 assumptions of schema_version=1 for every new record and version=event sequence superseded explicitly; legacy records/hashes remain unchanged
Database and process tests use only random owned disposable containers and test-only terminal seeds; race detector is not DB-correctness proof
No extra architecture Markdown or AGENTS files created; interim decisions live in this JSON, code and make help
Stage-02 audit found no runtime correctness defect; strengthened exact graph-limit, history-page and later-event rollback coverage
Process smoke waits for observed completed scans and new outage logs instead of assuming progress from fixed sleeps

03.title: Broker, outbox, workers, and basic leases
implemented_capabilities: additive attempts/workers/outbox schema
normalization v3 with frozen v1/v2 encodings
authenticated versioned Protobuf/gRPC coordination
transactional capacity admission and current-generation fencing
atomic expiry/LOST/requeue/exhaustion
NATS file-backed durable shared pull consumer
outbox relay publish outside locks
bounded noop/delay workers with renewal/drain
quarantine without raw payloads
real PostgreSQL/broker/process verification

broker_decision.redis_streams: AOF/RDB persistence and stream trimming; groups/XACK plus explicit pending recovery via XAUTOCLAIM. Familiar lightweight operation, but more recovery plumbing to learn/build here.
broker_decision.nats_jetstream: File storage, durable pull groups, explicit acknowledgments/AckWait redelivery, bounded age/size retention. Fits bounded diagnostic queues with a small operational footprint; teaches broker acknowledgments independently of DB execution ownership.
broker_decision.kafka: Replicated partition logs, consumer groups and offset commits; time/size retention and manual replay. Strong high-throughput ecosystem, but partition/KRaft/offset operations exceed current workload needs; throughput is not measured.
broker_decision.failure_limits: One server/file replica; retained volume survives restart, not node/disk loss. No replication claim.

decisions: Notification is a hint; durable ClaimTask authorizes diagnostics. Ack after claim/confirmed obsolete ownership; transient failure is delayed NAK.
At-least-once dispatch and potentially repeated execution, with fenced result acceptance; broker duplicate suppression is only an optimization.
Admission advisory lock -> workflow -> task -> worker -> attempt; workflow serialization preserves cancellation/history order; no DB lock spans RPC/broker waits.
Worker heartbeat is only a liveness hint; PostgreSQL clock and current attempt/generation fence all lease/result writes.
Three attempts maximum; expired attempt becomes LOST and atomically queues a new generation or fails on exhaustion.
Outcomes compare canonical object metadata and PostgreSQL JSONB equality; an accepted retry returns original receipt after expiry.
Authenticated TLS is required off-loopback; plaintext test mode is explicit and loopback-only. Worker identity derives from configured bearer credential.
Stage-02 no-execution/normalization-v2-only assumptions superseded; existing hashes, receipts, DAG immutability and dependency policy retained.
Old READY rows acquire first-generation outbox notifications in migration 00003; unowned pre-existing RUNNING rows cause an explicit upgrade refusal.
No arbitrary commands, paid models, GitHub writes or cloud provisioning; process fixtures are diagnostic only.
limitations: Stage 04 must add age-based READY republishing after broker data/retention loss; SENT outbox rows do not currently republish.
Single-node broker storage and per-workflow/global admission serialization limit availability/throughput; performance unmeasured.

04.title: Recovery, retries, cancellation, and backpressure
04.prerequisite_verification: Full verify-stage-03 passed before source changes, including real PostgreSQL/NATS failover and relay SIGKILL checks
implemented_capabilities: additive migration 00004; normalization v4 with frozen v1-v3 inputs
persisted max attempts, jittered retry due time, fixed overall deadlines and last error
bounded startup/periodic recovery and visible ownership consistency checks
CANCELLING stop acknowledgment or lease-fence settlement with residual cleanup evidence
diagnostic tool authorization and fenced results
transactional admission, READY limit and bounded capability mismatch handling
same-generation resend with distinct transport publication revision
bounded task/attempt inspection; manual redrive deferred
decisions: PostgreSQL clock after ownership locks governs expiry/deadline predicates. Heartbeats never revive leases.
Admission lock -> workflow -> task -> worker -> attempt. Scheduler READY admission uses the same global lock; no DB locks span broker/RPC waits.
Capacity is derived from durable RUNNING attempts, including stop-requested attempts until acknowledged or reaped. No decrement counter can run twice.
All instances sharing a database must use the same operator admission/concurrency configuration. Admission is serialized for correctness; throughput is unmeasured.
Retry time uses capped exponential equal jitter [cap/2,cap]; the sampled DB-time due date is stored once. RETRY_WAIT occupies no worker, long-lived transaction or timer.
Only transient_infrastructure/worker_lost retry. Permissions/configuration/unsupported/diagnostic failure are permanent. Explicit cancellation and deadline never retry.
New request timeout_ms fields (100ms-24h) and task max_attempts (1-10) require normalization v4; zero means omitted/default. Legacy v1-v3 hashes and receipts stay unchanged.
Persisted deadlines are measured from accepted creation, capped per workflow and immutable. Defaults are workflow 10m/task 2m/3 attempts; old rows get one bounded migration grace window.

CANCELLING denies new claims, tools and results. Renew signals stop without extending the lease. Settle on diagnostic stop acknowledgment or expired fenced ownership; retain cleanup_required when physical termination is unproven.

Acknowledging an old LOST attempt only clears its own cleanup flag with an audit event; it cannot change replacement outcomes or grant ownership. Cleanup audit events may advance a terminal workflow revision while its accepted outcome remains immutable.
Outbox task/generation uniqueness stays intact. READY resends reuse the logical generation but increase publish_revision, avoiding broker duplicate-window suppression after message loss.

Publish/fetch failures re-ensure configured JetStream streams and durable consumer under bounded contexts. Real broker tests delete both streams/consumer, then recover through existing client handles and same-generation dispatch.

Cancellation, terminal failure/completion and superseded generations mark unsent outbox rows OBSOLETE in the same transaction. Retained audit rows are excluded from the relay queue, preventing create/cancel cycles from bypassing queue bounds.
FIFO/age ordering and rotating workflow scans are initial policy; locks and per-workflow serialization provide no strict fairness or throughput guarantee.
Malformed notifications use bounded digest-only broker quarantine; exhausted logical tasks keep bounded classified DB attempts/events and read-only diagnostics.
Manual redrive, provider fallback and model/code repair loops are deferred. Future application-loop budgets must remain separate from infrastructure retry budgets.
Stage-03 immediate requeue/cancellation assumptions intentionally superseded by RETRY_WAIT/CANCELLING; earlier creation/cancellation timestamps, payloads and hash contracts retained.

The initial Docker-off failure was environmental; full Stage-03 baseline passed before changes. Stage-04 process tests then exposed a latent Stage-03 worker renewal-cancellation race: normal completion cancelled an in-flight renewal and falsely abandoned ownership. Fixed and covered by a controlled real-RPC renewal-reply regression.
Regression tests caught and repaired no-active cancellation timestamp/payload compatibility during this implementation; the original assertions remain enforced.
limitations: A DB fence is not proof that an old physical process or external side effect stopped. Stage 05 must enforce sandbox teardown and tool-side fencing.

Single-node file-backed JetStream survives process restart with retained volume, not node/disk loss; notification loss is recoverable from surviving PostgreSQL within configured resend/deadline budgets.
No manual redrive endpoint, provider fallback, model calls, cloud deployment, hostile-code isolation or measured throughput.
